notes:
Three of the ten named services have a confirmed feed: the Canadian Coast Guard (Canada.ca departmental Atom feed on api.io.canada.ca, 50 entries, newest 2026-10-15), Maritime New Zealand (RSS 2.0 at maritimenz.govt.nz/public/news/news-feed, 143 items, newest 21 October 2026) and KNRM (two RSS 2.0 feeds: rss/reddingrapporten, per-station rescue reports, 44 items, newest 17 October 2026; rss/nieuws, organisation news, 30 items, newest dated 13 October 2026 plus one future-dated 2027 event notice). A fourth working feed, surflifesaving.com.au/feed/, turned out to be Surf Life Saving NSW (a state member of SLSA), not Surf Life Saving Australia; it is recorded as evidence but not counted as SLSA. So the task is partial: 3 of the 5 required services (from the 10 named), plus one related state body. Of the other seven: gov.ie (Irish Coast Guard) and salvamentomaritimo.es refuse this fetcher by robots.txt; guardiacostiera.gov.it answers an error on every address (looks like a block on non-browser agents); sls.com.au, royallifesaving.com.au, seenotretter.de (TYPO3) and rs.no expose no RSS/Atom link on the pages that could be read. WebFetch cannot send custom headers, so 'needs a browser user agent' is an inference from the errors, not a tested fact; GitHub's runner may fare differently and should try each address once. The robots.txt refusals apply to this fetcher; a person should check whether those sites' robots.txt allow the watch's agent before any gov.ie or salvamentomaritimo.es address is added.

Watch compatibility, read against scripts/watch.mjs parseFeed: the Canada feed is Atom with <link href> and <updated>, which the parser handles. The Maritime NZ feed has no <pubDate> or <dc:date>; dates are only in <media-date> ('Wednesday, 21 October 2026', which Node's Date.parse reads), so items would be queued with published null unless the parser falls back to media-date. Both KNRM feeds are cut off before the closing channel and rss tags; the regex parser only takes complete <item> blocks so it still gets the items, but a strict XML parser would reject them. KNRM items are in Dutch and keywords.json is English-only, so nothing from KNRM would match until Dutch include patterns exist (for example vermist, te water, omgeslagen, gekapseisd, reddingsactie, verdronken). One KNRM nieuws item title names a private donor; the watch stores only a hash of titles, so the queue is unaffected, but a reviewer following the link will see a name.

Terms of use: none of the feeds carries a copyright or terms element. Canada.ca's terms page permits non-commercial reproduction with conditions (verify accuracy, credit the title and author, cite the source URL) and reserves commercial redistribution; it does not mention feeds. Site-wide terms for Maritime NZ, KNRM and SLS NSW were not checked within the fetch budget. The Maritime NZ feed's own self link names a second address, https://maritimenz.govt.nz/news-landing-page/news-feed, which was not fetched.

Suggested sources.json entries, all kind official: ccg-news (Canada), mnz-news (New Zealand), knrm-reddingrapporten and knrm-nieuws (Netherlands), slsnsw-news (Australia, NSW). Newest-item dates were read on 21 October 2026 through WebFetch, which obeys robots.txt and may behave differently from GitHub's runner. About 40 fetches and searches were used. VERIFICATION 21 Oct 2026: all five feeds re-fetched and parsed (Canada 50 entries, Maritime NZ 143, KNRM rescue reports 43 complete of 44, KNRM news 29 of 30, SLS NSW 9). Terms the first pass did not check: KNRM's disclaimer allows personal non-commercial use only and needs permission for reproduction; Maritime NZ's copyright page allows personal reuse with acknowledgement; SLS NSW's terms need SLSA's written consent for copying; none mentions feeds. The watch stores only links, dates, a kind and a title hash, which is the use these terms would need to be read against.
